newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber dips, trade says stocks exaggerated.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber dips, trade says stocks exaggerated.

text.p: Thai rubber prices dipped on Monday as buyers were sidelined by news that Thailand had stock levels of about 140,000 tonnes, trade sources said.
But many traders said the estimated private sector stock of 70,000 tonnes was exaggerated.
"I don't think the amount would exceed 20,000-30,000 tonnes. The figure apparently has had an effect on the trade today as buyers believed the price could dip further," said a Hat Yai trader.

Traders said a Thai industry official who attended a gathering of regional rubber producers on Indonesia's resort island of Bali over the weekend told the meeting Thai stock levels were about 140,000 tonnes, half each held by the government and private sector.
Traders said rubber prices should not be pressured much by this as long as the government refrained from unwinding its stock now.
However, some said there was market talk the government was about to sell the rubber.

"The talk also affected sentiment. Even though the government repeatedly reassured the market that it would not sell when prices were still bearish, players were sceptical as the government had recently done lots of things it said it wouldn't," said a Bangkok trader.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for December was indicated around 97.00 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok, down two cents from Monday. September was quoted around 98.00 US cents on the same basis, traders said.
